claims.statement: For qualifying heat-pump categories, current Czyste Powietrze rules require the specific device to be on List ZUM on the invoice or equivalent accounting-document date.
List ZUM placement is free and must be made by a manufacturer or another party holding the manufacturer's authority, limiting the service to evidence preparation, delegated support, and monitoring.
Accredited laboratory evidence remains material for the popular air-to-water category, while recognised quality marks and simplified conditions reduce complexity for other heat-pump categories.

The 2025 EPREL reconciliation created substantial update work and temporary suspension risk, but EPREL already provides supplier workflows and public/API access, so this is evidence of operational pain rather than proprietary access.

Adjacent Polish compliance providers already sell documentation checking and EPREL registration help, demonstrating a service substitute and some category willingness to outsource, but not recurring heat-pump monitoring demand.

contrary_evidence: The official List ZUM workflow is free, public, and accepts supplier submissions directly.
The April 2025 rule change simplified evidence for several heat-pump categories, reducing the universal complexity thesis.
EPREL supplies registration guidance, generated labels, and public/API access, reducing the need for a standalone data layer.
RCC already offers adjacent EPREL documentation and registration support, while accredited laboratories hold the strongest evidence relationship.
The large 2025 update backlog was tied to a specific migration deadline and does not establish recurring monthly pain.

economics.acquisition_route: Evidence-constrained hypothesis: obtain introductions from one accredited testing laboratory, one adjacent EPREL documentation provider, and the founder's family HVAC channel; no referral commitment has been observed.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The Polish ZUM wedge alone is not evidenced to support the founder's wealth objective. A plausible path would require proving roughly 100-150 recurring supplier relationships at about 20000-30000 PLN annual revenue each, then expanding the same evidence operations into additional EU energy-labelling and subsidy registers; that scale, retention, and 6-9 year timing are hypotheses rather than findings.
economics.founder_time: 10-16 hours weekly for a document-only pilot, with accredited testing and specialist interpretation purchased rather than performed by the founder
economics.gross_margin_basis: Evidence-refined hypothesis: 55-70% blended gross margin after translation and specialist review; software-only margins are unlikely before evidence templates stabilise
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 12-24 months if 6-10 model-family projects are sold without building a full platform first
economics.pricing: Evidence-refined hypothesis: 4000-10000 PLN per model family for preflight and coordination, plus 400-1200 PLN monthly per supplier for monitoring; official List ZUM placement itself is free and no direct willingness-to-pay evidence supports the discovery price.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Potential repeats arise from new model families, EPREL or label changes, rule amendments, and suspension remediation; the observed 2025 EPREL clean-up proves episodic update work but not stable monthly demand.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: With permission, a corpus of report-field mappings, model-family equivalence decisions, EPREL mismatches, and observed update requests could shorten later preflights; no evidence yet shows that this corpus would be exclusive or defensible against laboratories and compliance consultancies.
fingerprint.customer: Non-Polish heat-pump manufacturers, authorised representatives, and Polish importers with multiple model variants seeking subsidised Polish sales
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Referral or white-label delivery through accredited heat-pump laboratories, Polish master distributors, and adjacent EPREL compliance firms, subject to partner validation
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Fixed-fee evidence preflight and authorised submission support, followed by optional low-touch status and rule-change monitoring
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The EU supplier, authorised representative, or importer pays when releasing a model family into Poland, correcting a material mismatch, or refreshing a catalogue after a rule change
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A specific model must be visible on List ZUM on the invoice date while the submitted identifiers and evidence must remain aligned with laboratory, energy-label, and EPREL records

founder_fit: The family renewable-installation business can help test invoice-date and model-identifier failure modes without using employer-confidential information.
Document extraction, reconciliation, and monitoring fit the founder's data-science and AI leverage.
A fixed-scope service pilot can run part-time and without camera-led distribution.
The founder lacks accredited heat-pump testing and regulatory sign-off capability, so expert scope boundaries and paid review are mandatory.
risks: Programme funding or eligibility rules can change abruptly and compress the addressable market.
Advice may be mistaken for approval or certification unless contracts and interface copy allocate responsibility clearly.
Laboratories, master distributors, or existing product-compliance firms can absorb the workflow.
Supplier reports and product roadmaps are commercially sensitive and require strict permissioning and EU data controls.
A Poland-only register may not produce enough recurring revenue to support a scalable standalone company.

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulatory evidence operations service with a lightweight monitoring workspace
structure.control_point: The supplier-approved model-family evidence pack immediately before List ZUM submission or update
structure.critical_dependency: Continued subsidy relevance, supplier authorisation and report access, plus demonstrable reduction in rework beyond the free official workflow

thesis: A narrowly scoped managed preflight and monitoring service could help non-Polish heat-pump manufacturers, their authorised representatives, and Polish importers reconcile laboratory reports, EPREL records, energy labels, model-family identifiers, and the current List ZUM form before the customer submits. The service would organise evidence and alert on mismatches or status changes; it would not perform tests, own the supplier's legal declarations, or promise listing. Official submission is free, the public workflow is usable without proprietary software, and adjacent compliance firms already prepare EPREL documentation, so willingness to pay for a recurring layer remains unvalidated.
title: ZUM Evidence Gate for Heat-Pump Suppliers
uncertainties: Number of distinct paying suppliers behind the thousands of listed model variants
Actual first-pass rejection, correction, suspension, and model-update frequency after the 2025 migration
Whether laboratories or distributors will refer rather than internalise the service
Public or permitted machine-readable access to every status and document needed for reliable monitoring
Verified price sensitivity among non-Polish OEMs, importers, and authorised representatives
